CHIEF COMPLAINT
===============
Syncope

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
==========================
80-year-old woman with aortic stenosis who presents after a syncopal episode while climbing stairs. She reports 2 months of exertional dyspnea and one prior near-syncopal episode. Today she lost consciousness for ~30 seconds, no seizure activity, no incontinence, spontaneous recovery. Denies chest pain, palpitations. Witness (daughter) confirms brief loss of consciousness.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
===================
Severe aortic stenosis (valve area 0.8 cm2), hypertension, hypothyroidism.

MEDICATION LIST
===============
* Levothyroxine 75 mcg daily
* Amlodipine 5 mg daily
* Atorvastatin 20 mg nightly

SOCIAL HISTORY
==============
Widowed, lives with daughter. Independent in ADLs. No tobacco, no alcohol.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
====================
Vital signs: Temp 97.9 F, HR 72, BP 108/68, RR 16, SpO2 95% RA.
Cardiovascular: Harsh crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur at right upper sternal border radiating to carotids, delayed carotid upstroke.
Lungs: Clear.
Neurologic: Nonfocal.

DIAGNOSTIC DATA
===============
Labs: BNP 890, Hgb 11.8, Creatinine 1.2.
EKG: Left ventricular hypertrophy with strain pattern.
Echocardiogram: Severe aortic stenosis, mean gradient 48 mmHg, EF 55%.

IMPRESSION
==========
80-year-old woman with syncope secondary to severe aortic stenosis.

RECOMMENDATIONS
==============
1. Symptomatic severe aortic stenosis with syncope
   - Cardiology and cardiothoracic surgery consults for valve replacement evaluation
   - Avoid vigorous exertion, counsel on syncope precautions
2. Hypertension
   - Continue amlodipine; monitor for hypotension
3. Hypothyroidism
   - Continue levothyroxine; TSH on file from last month
